messages:
ops-bot: 🚨 ALERT: SLO breach detected for dedicated pool `dedicated-prod-3` - paging @oncall-jin. p95=820ms (SLO=200ms), p99=2.3s (SLO=500ms), queue_depth=420, streaming stalls observed. Autoscaler latency: 120s since scale request. Link: /incidents/1780001234

Jin Park: Got the page, I'm looking. Confirming scope: is this affecting hosted customers or only Dedicated customers on pool dedicated-prod-3?

Maya Li: Only dedicated-prod-3 so far. CS reports 2 enterprise customers on that pool experiencing degraded tail latency and streaming stalls.

Ravi Patel: Logs show a pattern: incoming burst at 12:03:15 UTC, continuous requests with long KV cache misses. Autoscaler accepted request to add 4 nodes at 12:03:20 but instances didn't become Ready until ~12:05:20. Warmup scripts show model shards still loading, and gRPC handshake delays.

Jin Park: Can someone paste the autoscaler event log and the nodepool state?

Ravi Patel: Pasting snippets:
```
[12:03:20] autoscaler: scale_request(pool=dedicated-prod-3, add=4)
[12:03:21] k8s: creating node node-87
[12:03:35] node-87: kubelet started
[12:04:10] node-87: docker runtime ready
[12:05:05] runtime: model load started (shard 0)
[12:05:18] node-87: Ready
[12:05:20] autoscaler: scale_complete
```
Also seeing warmup timeout logs from runtime: `warmup: kv_cache_init timed out after 45s` on two nodes.

Lina Gomez: Customer notice: "we saw streaming stall where the stream froze for ~6s then resumed, some completions truncated". They are asking for ETA for mitigation.

Jin Park: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Divert new requests to fallback model variant (lighter quantized) on us-east-1, 2) Reduce batch size and disable multi-request batching on affected pool, 3) Manually scale dedicated-prod-3 by +2 nodes to relieve queue quickly. Who can run the scale?

Maya Li: I'll run the manual scale and change routing. Doing: `redwoodctl pools scale --name dedicated-prod-3 --add 2 --reason "incident surge"`

deploy-bot: Command accepted. Job ID: job-55321. Nodes provisioning.

Maya Li: Also applied traffic-split: set 25% to fallback-quantized variant for new requests. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing set-split --pool dedicated-prod-3 --variant fallback-quant --weight 25
```

Priya Nair: Noted. CS updated customers: "we've shifted a portion of traffic to a lower-latency fallback and are scaling; immediate impact should be visible in ~2-3m".

Ravi Patel: Added runtime tweak: disabled request-level batching on dedicated-prod-3 so individual requests don't get queued into big batches while nodes warm. Command applied to service config.

Jin Park: Observability — Lina, can you share live p95/p99 after changes?

Lina Gomez: Metrics updating... p95 dropped to 460ms within 90s, p99 still ~980ms. Queue depth down to 210. Streaming stall reports reduced but one customer still seeing 4-5s pauses.

Ravi Patel: I can see a tail of requests still routed to busy nodes where KV cache miss penalty is high. We'll temporarily enable KV prefix cache preload on new nodes to speed warmup. Patch: set `kv_cache.preload=true` for new nodepool.

Jin Park: Apply and monitor. If p99 < 600ms and queue < 100 we're in recovery state.

Maya Li: KV preload flag set. Nodes finishing model load now. Deploy-bot: node-88 Ready at 12:06:20. Node-89 Ready at 12:06:45.

deploy-bot: job-55321 completed. New capacity online.

Lina Gomez: Updated metrics: p95=190ms, p99=480ms, queue_depth=48, streaming stalls back to baseline. Customers confirmed degraded experience mostly resolved. :white_check_mark:

Sam Ortiz: Thanks team. Can we capture the timeline + root cause? My notes: burst > expected, autoscaler request accepted but provisioning + model warmup took ~2m causing tail spikes. Warmup failures due to KV cache init timeout increased latency on new nodes which amplified queueing.

Ravi Patel: Agreed. Root cause: autoscaler still healthy but warmup heuristics are too slow for hot bursts (model load + kv init > autoscaler expected window). Also batch sizing policy combined with large queue contributed to tail latency.

Jin Park: Action items (creating follow-up):
- Investigate autoscaler warmup thresholds & reduce expected ready time for dedicated pools.
- Add an alert: queue_depth > 250 for any dedicated pool (warn at 150).
- Ensure fallback routing policy can flip to 50% automatically if queue > 300.
- Improve KV cache preload by default for pools with high burst risk.
- Postmortem doc + customer-facing summary.

Priya Nair: I'll draft the customer note and coordinate with Sam for messaging.

Maya Li: I'll own the autoscaler warmup follow-up with Ravi. Assigning to sprint.

Jin Park: Great. Incident moving to mitigated. We'll keep this thread for P0->P1 handoff and the postmortem. Thanks all. :bow:
